newsitem.title: USA: U.S. protests to Russia over American spy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. protests to Russia over American spy.

text.p: The United States has protested to Russia over the activities of a CIA official accused of selling secrets to Moscow, calling the incident unacceptable, the State Department said on Tuesday.

Spokesman Glyn Davies said diplomatic protests had been lodged both in Washington and Moscow following the arrest by U.S. authorities of Harold Nicholson, a 16-year veteran of the Central Intelligence Agency.
Davies told reporters Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbott had called Russian ambassador Yuli Vorontsov, while the U.S. embassy had delivered a similar protest in Moscow.
"The message of course was that we view this activity as unacceptable, and we reserve the right to take further action," he said. Davies declined to say what that action might be.

Davies said Washington viewed the incident as "inconsistent with the pattern of bilateral relations of recent years. We have demanded an explanation ... and made clear that we are considering appropriate measures," he said.
In Moscow, a foreign ministry spokesman said Russia viewed the incident as an internal matter of the United States "and we have nothing to do with it".
